title: Gravitational Accessory Fitting Simulator
description: A sculpted head (LeePerrySmith) floats at the center of the scene while a rolex watch and a corset orbit around it under simulated gravity. The user must carefully adjust gravitational strength, orbital velocity, drag coefficients, and launch angles to guide each accessory into its correct docking position on the head — the watch onto the forehead like a crown and the corset around the neck like a collar — triggering a satisfying snap-lock animation upon successful placement.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a gravitational accessory fitting simulator. Load three GLB models using GLTFLoader: LeePerrySmith.glb as a central sculpted head, rolex.glb as an orbiting watch, and Corset.glb as an orbiting corset. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 6) looking at the origin with OrbitControls for scene inspection. Add ambient light intensity 0.5 and a directional light at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 1.2 and shadow mapping enabled. Scale the head to roughly 2 units tall centered at origin. Scale the rolex to about 0.4 units and the corset to about 0.6 units. Both accessories start orbiting the head at radius 3 with random initial angles. Implement a custom physics loop: each accessory has properties for orbitalVelocity, gravitationalPull (toward the head center), dragCoefficient, and radialOffset. Create an HTML overlay panel with sliders for: (1) gravity strength 0-5, (2) watch orbital speed 0-3, (3) corset orbital speed 0-3, (4) drag coefficient 0-1, (5) a launch angle slider 0-360 for each object. Add a 'Release' button for each accessory that stops its orbit and lets it fall inward under the current gravity. Define two invisible target zones as small spheres: one at the forehead position (0, 1.2, 0.5) for the watch and one at the neck position (0, -0.5, 0.3) for the corset. When a released accessory enters within 0.3 units of its target, snap it into place with a short tween animation (scale bounce and glow effect using emissive material flash). Track successful dockings and display a status HUD showing docked/undocked state for each item. If an accessory misses and falls below y=-5, reset it to orbit. Validate that gravity is above 0.5 and drag is below 0.8 before allowing release. The full interaction requires adjusting parameters, releasing the watch, potentially resetting, adjusting again, releasing the corset, achieving both docks. Use requestAnimationFrame for the physics update loop with delta time clamped to 60fps equivalent.
